rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi links the verse to passages describing angels taking disbelievers and God's messengers taking souls.
rows.anchor: ولو ترى إذ يتوفى الذين كفروا الملائكة [الأنفال: 50]، وقال تعالى: { توفته رسلنا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is the true creator and agent of every act; He gives life, brings death, and takes souls, as other verses state.
rows.anchor: والبارىء خالق الكل، الفاعل حقيقة لكل فعل قال الله تعالى: { الله يتوفى الأنفس حين موتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Angel of Death takes souls directly, his assistants handle them, and God ultimately takes the spirit; the act is attributed to the angel because he is entrusted with its direct execution, as creation can be attributed to an angel.
rows.anchor: فملك الموت يقبض والأعوان يعالجون والله تعالى يزهق الروح. وهذا هو الجمع بين الآي والأحاديث

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid compares the world before the Angel of Death to a basin before a person, from which he takes wherever he wishes.
rows.anchor: وروي عن مجاهد أن الدنيا بين يدي ملك الموت كالطست بين يدي الإنسان يأخذ من حيث شاء

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Qurtubi says the comparison of the world to a basin before the Angel of Death was also reported as a Prophetic narration; he gives no grading here.
rows.anchor: وقد روي هذا المعنى مرفوعا، وقد ذكرناه في كتاب التذكرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the Angel of Death complained that people blame and curse him; God said He would make death appear to result from illnesses so people would speak well of him.
rows.anchor: وروي أن ملك الموت لما وكله الله تعالى بقبض الأرواح قال: رب جعلتني أذكر بسوء ويشتمني بنو آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi says the Angel of Death summons souls, takes them, and hands them to the angels of mercy or punishment; he refers readers to his Tadhkira for details.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكرنا أنه يدعو الأرواح فتجيئه ويقبضها، ثم يسلمها إلى ملائكة الرحمة أو العذاب بما فيه شفاء

rows.speaker: بعض العلماء
rows.claim: Some scholars infer from the wording that agency is permissible, since the Angel of Death is appointed to take souls.
rows.anchor: استدل بهذه الآية بعض العلماء على جواز الوكالة من قوله: { وكل بكم } أي بقبض الأرواح

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi rejects deriving ordinary legal agency from this wording alone: the purposes differ, just as God's commissioning a Messenger or commanding alms does not establish those analogies.
rows.anchor: قال ابن العربي: «وهذا أخذ من لفظه لا من معناه، ولو اطرد ذلك لقلنا في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: If the verse is read for its meaning, Ibn al-Arabi says it supports a judge appointing someone to seize a due right by force, without the debtor's act or consent.
rows.anchor: أما إنه إذا لم يكن بد من المعاني فيقال: إن هذه الآية دليل على أن للقاضي أن يستنيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause beginning “if you saw” is a subject with its predicate supplied by the following construction, according to Qurtubi.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: { ولو ترى إذ المجرمون ناكسوا رءوسهم عند ربهم } ابتداء وخبر

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the address to the Prophet is also an address to his community: Muhammad would see the deniers of resurrection on Judgment Day and witness an astonishing scene.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: والمخاطبة للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مخاطبة لأمته. والمعنى: ولو ترى يا محمد منكري البعث

rows.speaker: أبو العباس
rows.claim: Abu al-Abbas proposes that Muhammad is told to say to a criminal that, if he saw the criminals bowing their heads before their Lord, he would regret his past conduct.
rows.anchor: ومذهب أبي العباس غير هذا، وأن يكون المعنى: يا محمد، قل للمجرم ولو ترى إذ المجرمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their bowed heads express regret, disgrace, grief, humiliation, and anguish.
rows.anchor: «ناكسو رءوسهم» أي من الندم والخزي والحزن والذل والغم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are before their Lord at the reckoning and recompense for their deeds.
rows.anchor: «عند ربهم» أي عند محاسبة ربهم وجزاء أعمالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Our Lord” introduces what the criminals are saying.
rows.anchor: «ربنا» أي يقولون ربنا. «أبصرنا» أي أبصرنا ما كنا نكذب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They now see what they used to deny and hear what they used to reject.
rows.anchor: «أبصرنا» أي أبصرنا ما كنا نكذب. «وسمعنا» ما كنا ننكر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative gloss says they saw the truth of God's threat and heard confirmation of His messengers.
rows.anchor: وقيل: «أبصرنا» صدق وعيدك. «وسمعنا» تصديق رسلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They see and hear when those faculties can no longer benefit them; in worldly life they perceived but failed to reflect, as though blind and deaf, then awakened in the hereafter.
rows.anchor: أبصروا حين لا ينفعهم البصر، وسمعوا حين لا ينفعهم السمع. «فارجعنا» أي إلى الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask to be returned to worldly life.
rows.anchor: «فارجعنا» أي إلى الدنيا. { نعمل صالحا إنا موقنون }

rows.speaker: النقاش
rows.claim: Al-Naqqash says they now affirm belief in the resurrection.
rows.anchor: أي مصدقون بالبعث قاله النقاش. وقيل: مصدقون بالذي جاء به محمد

rows.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
rows.claim: Yahya ibn Salam says they now believe that Muhammad brought the truth.
rows.anchor: مصدقون بالذي جاء به محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه حق قاله يحيى بن سلام

rows.speaker: سفيان الثوري
rows.claim: Sufyan al-Thawri says God refutes their request with the statement that, if returned, they would relapse into what they were forbidden to do and would be lying.
rows.anchor: قال سفيان الثوري: فأكذبهم الله تعالى فقال: ولو ردوا لعادوا لما نهوا عنه وإنهم لكاذبون

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation makes their certainty the removal of doubts: they had seen and heard in life but did not reflect, and only now became alert.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معنى «إنا موقنون» أي قد زالت عنا الشكوك الآن وكانوا يسمعون ويبصرون في الدنيا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further reading takes their words as admitting that they saw God's messengers and marvels of creation and heard the messengers, leaving them without an excuse before they request return.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أي ربنا لك الحجة، فقد أبصرنا رسلك وعجائب خلقك في الدنيا، وسمعنا كلامهم

rows.speaker: الحسن وأبو العالية والضحاك وأبي بن كعب وإبراهيم النخعي وابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Hasan, Abu al-Aliya, al-Dahhak, Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, and Ibn Abbas identify the lesser torment as worldly afflictions and illnesses that test people until they repent.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن وأبو العالية والضحاك وأبي بن كعب وإبراهيم النخعي: العذاب الأدنى مصائب الدنيا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas also identifies the lesser torment as the prescribed legal penalties.
rows.anchor: وعنه أيضا أنه الحدود. وقال ابن مسعود والحسين بن علي وعبد الله بن الحارث

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود والحسين بن علي وعبد الله بن الحارث
rows.claim: Ibn Mas'ud, al-Husayn ibn Ali, and Abdullah ibn al-Harith say the lesser torment was being killed by the sword at Badr.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود والحسين بن علي وعبد الله بن الحارث: هو القتل بالسيف يوم بدر

rows.speaker: مقاتل ومجاهد
rows.claim: Maqatil and Mujahid identify it as the seven-year famine in Mecca, when people ate carrion.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: الجوع سبع سنين بمكة حتى أكلوا الجيف وقاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: مجاهد والبراء بن عازب
rows.claim: Mujahid and al-Bara ibn Azib are also cited for identifying the lesser torment as punishment in the grave.
rows.anchor: وعنه أيضا: العذاب الأدنى عذاب القبر وقاله البراء بن عازب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi says the greater torment is generally agreed to be Hell, while reporting Ja'far ibn Muhammad's exception that it is the Mahdi's emergence with the sword; one report identifies the lesser torment as high prices.
rows.anchor: ولا خلاف أن العذاب الأكبر عذاب جهنم إلا ما روي عن جعفر بن محمد أنه خروج المهدي بالسيف

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayri reports an interpretation of the lesser torment as punishment in the grave but questions it because the verse says the torment may make them return.
rows.anchor: قال القشيري: وقيل عذاب القبر. وفيه نظر لقوله: { لعلهم يرجعون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For those who understand the lesser torment as killing, “so that they may return” means those who survive may turn back.
rows.anchor: ومن حمل العذاب على القتل قال: { لعلهم يرجعون } أي يرجع من بقي منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For Mujahid's and al-Bara's view, the phrase can mean that people wish for and ask to return; the passive reading supports this, as does the usage that names an intended act as if performed.
rows.anchor: وقد قيل: إن معنى قوله: { لعلهم يرجعون } على قول مجاهد والبراء: أي لعلهم يريدون الرجوع ويطلبونه

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Qurtubi invokes a Tirmidhi-reported Prophetic teaching that the heart receives a prompting from an angel and a prompting from Satan; he says the report was discussed in al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: لمة من الملك ولمة من الشيطان كما قال صلى الله عليه وسلم. خرجه الترمذي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heart is the site of thoughts and whispers, disbelief and faith, persistence and repentance, agitation and tranquility; these opposites cannot coexist in one heart, literally or figuratively.
rows.anchor: وهو محل الخطرات والوساوس ومكان الكفر والإيمان، وموضع الإصرار والإنابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The assertion that no man has two hearts also rebuts the previously mentioned hypocrites: there is one heart, containing faith or disbelief, not an intermediate degree of hypocrisy; people also quote it as an excuse for forgetting or confusion.
rows.anchor: أعلم الله عز وجل في هذه الآية أنه لا أحد بقلبين، ويكون في هذا طعن على المنافقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means a man tells his wife, “You are to me like my mother's back”; the ruling is treated in Surat al-Mujadila.
rows.anchor: يعني قول الرجل لامرأته: أنت علي كظهر أمي. وذلك مذكور في سورة «المجادلة»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exegetes agree that the ruling was revealed concerning Zayd ibn Haritha; Ibn Umar reports that people had called him Zayd ibn Muhammad until this verse came down.
rows.anchor: أجمع أهل التفسير على أن هذا نزل في زيد بن حارثة. وروى الأئمة أن ابن عمر قال

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك وغيره
rows.claim: A report says Zayd was captured in Syria by raiders from Tihama, bought by Hakim ibn Hizam, given to Khadija, then given to Muhammad, who freed and adopted him; when his father and uncle came seeking ransom, Zayd chose to stay, and Muhammad publicly declared him his son and heir.
rows.anchor: وكان زيد فيما روي عن أنس بن مالك وغيره مسبيا من الشام، سبته خيل من تهامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse concerning Zayd ended adoption as a recognized basis for inheritance and mutual support, and directs people to the known biological father as the more just attribution.
rows.anchor: وفي قول ابن عمر: ما كنا ندعو زيد بن حارثة إلا زيد بن محمد، دليل على أن التبني كان معمولا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In pre-Islamic practice, a man might adopt someone whose appearance or character pleased him, grant him a son's share of inheritance, and call him his son.
rows.anchor: كان الرجل في الجاهلية إذا أعجبه من الرجل جلده وظرفه ضمه إلى نفسه، وجعل له نصيب الذكر

rows.speaker: النحاس
rows.claim: Al-Nahhas calls the verse abrogation of the former adoption practice, a case of Qur'an abrogating Sunna: use the known father, otherwise known patronal affiliation, and otherwise brotherhood in religion.
rows.anchor: وقال النحاس: هذه الآية ناسخة لما كانوا عليه من التبني، وهو من نسخ السنة بالقرآن

words: وَلَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌۭ فِيمَآ أَخْطَأْتُم بِهِۦ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no sin when the tongue mistakenly gives someone an adoptive father's name; Qatada also exempts addressing someone as another's son when one believes that man is his father.
rows.anchor: لو نسبه إنسان إلى أبيه من التبني فإن كان على جهة الخطأ، وهو أن يسبق لسانه إلى ذلك

words: وَلَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌۭ فِيمَآ أَخْطَأْتُم بِهِۦ
rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says mistakenly calling a man the son of someone believed to be his father is covered by the verse's lifting of blame.
rows.anchor: قاله قتادة. ولا يجري هذا المجرى ما غلب عليه اسم التبني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Established names from prior adoption continued for people such as al-Miqdad ibn Amr, known as Ibn al-Aswad, and Salim mawla Abi Hudhayfa; Qurtubi distinguishes them from Zayd, whom one may not deliberately call Zayd ibn Muhammad.
rows.anchor: فإن الأسود بن عبد يغوث كان قد تبناه في الجاهلية وعرف به. فلما نزلت الآية قال المقداد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Deliberately calling Zayd ibn Haritha “Zayd ibn Muhammad” is sinful; Qurtubi reads God as forgiving deliberate wrong and merciful by removing the penalty for accidental error.
rows.anchor: فإن قاله أحد متعمدا عصى لقوله تعالى: { ولكن ما تعمدت قلوبكم } أي فعليكم الجناح

words: وَلَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌۭ فِيمَآ أَخْطَأْتُم بِهِۦ
rows.speaker: عطاء وكثير من العلماء
rows.claim: A group including Ata treats the clause broadly: one who swears not to leave a creditor until paid, accepts coins thought good, and then finds them counterfeit bears no liability.
rows.anchor: وكانت فتيا عطاء وكثير من العلماء. على هذا إذا حلف رجل ألا يفارق غريمه حتى يستوفي منه حقه

words: وَلَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌۭ فِيمَآ أَخْطَأْتُم بِهِۦ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Under the broad reading of accidental error, someone who swears not to greet a person but greets him unknowingly has not broken the oath.
rows.anchor: وكذلك عنده إذا حلف ألا يسلم على فلان فسلم عليه وهو لا يعرفه أنه لا يحنث

words: مَّآ أَخْطَأْتُم بِهِۦ وَلَٰكِن مَّا تَعَمَّدَتْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second “ma” may be genitive by coordination with the first “ma”; alternatively it is nominative after an implied subject, “what you are answerable for is what your hearts intended.”
rows.anchor: و«ما» في موضع خفض ردا على «ما» التي مع «أخطأتم». ويجوز أن تكون في موضع رفع

words: وَلَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌۭ فِيمَآ أَخْطَأْتُم بِهِۦ
rows.speaker: قتادة وغيره
rows.claim: Qatada and others say that mistakenly attributing a man to someone believed to be his father is among the errors for which God removed blame; another view is simply addressing someone as “my son” without adopting him.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة وغيره: من نسب رجلا إلى غير أبيه، وهو يرى أنه أبوه، خطأ فذلك من الذي رفع الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “With your mouths” emphasizes that the claim has no reality and is only something said; “I walk to you on my foot” is a comparable expression of benevolence.
rows.anchor: «بأفواهكم» تأكيد لبطلان القول أي أنه قول لا حقيقة له في الوجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Al-haqq” is an adjective for an omitted verbal noun: God speaks the true speech.
rows.anchor: «الحق» نعت لمصدر محذوف أي يقول القول الحق. و { يهدي } معناه يبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here “yahdi” means “clarifies” and takes a direct object without a preposition.
rows.anchor: و { يهدي } معناه يبين فهو يتعدى بغير حرف جر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adiya is the plural of da'i, someone called the son of a man other than his father or claiming someone other than his father; the verbal noun is da'wa, with a kasra. Unknown lineage makes one a patron and brother in religion.
rows.anchor: الأدعياء جمع الدعي، وهو الذي يدعى ابنا لغير أبيه أو يدعي غير أبيه والمصدر الدعوة بالكسر

rows.speaker: أبو بكرة
rows.claim: Al-Tabari reports Abu Bakra reading the verse and saying that, since his father was unknown, he was the Muslims' brother in religion and patron; the narrator says Abu Bakra would have claimed even a donkey as father if he knew it. Hadith transmitters call him Nufay ibn al-Harith.
rows.anchor: وذكر الطبري أن أبا بكرة قرأ هذه الآية وقال: أنا ممن لا يعرف أبوه، فأنا أخوكم في الدين

rows.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص وأبو بكرة
rows.claim: A report in the Sahih collections, from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas and Abu Bakra, says the Prophet declared Paradise forbidden to one who knowingly claims a father other than his own.
rows.anchor: روى الصحيح عن سعد بن أبي وقاص وأبي بكرة كلاهما قال: سمعته أذناي ووعاه قلبي محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: أبو ذر
rows.claim: Abu Dharr reports the Prophet saying that a man who knowingly claims a father other than his own commits disbelief; Qurtubi gives no grading here.
rows.anchor: وفي حديث أبي ذر أنه سمع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since idols own nothing of what God can do, Muhammad is told to ask who provides from heaven and earth: rain, sun, moon, stars and their benefits, and earthly water and plants. Idols cannot claim these works; if the polytheists admit God provides, they concede He alone should be worshipped.
rows.anchor: لما ذكر أن آلهتهم لا يملكون مثقال ذرة مما يقدر عليه الرب قرر ذلك فقال: قل يا محمد للمشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “either we or you” wording presents the case with apparent fairness, like saying one of us is lying while knowing oneself truthful; it indirectly declares the two camps opposed, with the Prophet's side guided and the polytheists astray.
rows.anchor: هذا على وجه الإنصاف في الحجة كما يقول القائل: أحدنا كاذب، وهو يعلم أنه صادق

words: لَعَلَىٰ هُدًى أَوْ فِى ضَلَٰلٍۢ مُّبِينٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two sides cannot share one position: one is guided and the other plainly astray; Qurtubi identifies the Prophet's side as guided and the polytheists as astray for associating partners with their provider.
rows.anchor: بل على أمرين متضادين، وأحد الفريقين مهتد وهو نحن والآخر ضال وهو أنتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Iyyakum” coordinates with the subject of inna; coordinating to its syntactic position would instead give “aw antum.” Qurtubi says the first side alone is preferred for “upon guidance” in the former construction, though al-Mubarrad permits the first side in either analysis.
rows.anchor: «أو إياكم» معطوف على اسم «إن» ولو عطف على الموضع لكان «أو أنتم»

rows.speaker: البصريون
rows.claim: The Basran grammarians take “aw” in its ordinary disjunctive sense, not as doubt: Arabs use it this way when the speaker knows the answer but chooses not to state it.
rows.anchor: و«أو» عند البصريين على بابها وليست للشك، ولكنها على ما تستعمله العرب

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة والفراء
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda and al-Farra say “aw” means “and,” yielding: we are guided and you are in manifest error.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة والفراء: هي بمعنى الواو، وتقديره: وإنا على هدى وإياكم في ضلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi glosses the preceding Jarir line as referring to Thalaba and Riyah.
rows.anchor: يعني أثعلبة ورياحا. وقال آخر:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi cites an unnamed poet's line, where “aw” joins Riyah and Rizam, as a further usage of the particle.
rows.anchor: فلما اشتد أمر الحرب فينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “A jramna” means “we acquired” or “committed.”
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: { قل لا تسألون عمآ أجرمنا } أي اكتسبنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speaker seeks the audience's good, not protection from any harm their disbelief might cause him; both sides will be recompensed. The wording resembles “you have your religion and I have mine.”
rows.anchor: أي إنما أقصد بما أدعوكم إليه الخير لكم، لا أنه ينالني ضرر كفركم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi calls this a verse of truce and disengagement, abrogated by the sword; another view is that it was revealed before the sword verse.
rows.anchor: فهذه آية مهادنة ومتاركة، وهي منسوخة بالسيف. وقيل: نزل هذا قبل آية السيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If people call on the idols for help in hardship, the idols cannot hear because they are inanimate and neither see nor hear.
rows.anchor: أي إن تستغيثوا بهم في النوائب لا يسمعوا دعاءكم لأنها جمادات لا تبصر ولا تسمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if they heard, hearing alone does not make every hearer able to speak or answer.
rows.anchor: إذ ليس كل سامع ناطقا. وقال قتادة: المعنى لو سمعوا لم ينفعوكم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada explains that even if the idols heard, they would not benefit their worshippers.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: المعنى لو سمعوا لم ينفعوكم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another hypothetical view says that even if given life and understanding, the idols would be more obedient to God than their worshippers and would not answer a call to disbelief.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أي لو جعلنا لهم عقولا وحياة فسمعوا دعاءكم لكانوا أطوع لله منكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Judgment Day the objects of worship will deny that their worshippers worshipped them and disavow them.
rows.anchor: أي يجحدون أنكم عبدتموهم، ويتبرءون منكم. ثم يجوز أن يرجع هذا إلى المعبودين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reference may include beings capable of understanding—angels, jinn, prophets, and devils—who deny that worship was right or that they ordered it, as Jesus says in the cited verse.
rows.anchor: مما يعقل كالملائكة والجن والأنبياء والشياطين أي يجحدون أن يكون ما فعلتموه حقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reference may also include idols: God will resurrect them so they can testify that they were unworthy of worship.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يندرج فيه الأصنام أيضا، أي يحييها الله حتى تخبر أنها ليست أهلا للعبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “all-knowing expert” is God: no one knows God's creation better than God, so no one can inform you about His work as He does.
rows.anchor: هو الله جل وعز أي لا أحد أخبر بخلق الله من الله، فلا ينبئك مثله في عمله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People need God for their continued existence and in every circumstance.
rows.anchor: أي المحتاجون إليه في بقائكم وكل أحوالكم. الزمخشري: «فإن قلت لم عرف الفقراء

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains the definite “the needy” as showing that people, through the severity of their need and weakness, constitute the class of the needy, though all creatures depend on God; an indefinite form would mean only some needy people.
rows.anchor: قصد بذلك أن يريهم أنهم لشدة افتقارهم إليه هم جنس الفقراء، وإن كانت الخلائق كلهم مفتقرين

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says “the Praiseworthy” adds that wealth alone does not benefit others: God is generous and beneficent through His wealth, so recipients owe Him praise.
rows.anchor: لما أثبت فقرهم إليه وغناه عنهم، وليس كل غني نافعا بغناه إلا إذا كان الغني جوادا منعما

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalil considers easing the second of the two hamzas the best pronunciation; easing only the first, easing both, or pronouncing both fully are also allowed.
rows.anchor: وتخفيف الهمزة الثانية أجود الوجوه عند الخليل، ويجوز تخفيف الأولى وحدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Huwa” may be an extra particle with no syntactic position, or the beginning of a nominal sentence and thus nominative.
rows.anchor: تكون «هو» زائدة، فلا يكون لها موضع من الإعراب، وتكون مبتدأة فيكون موضعها رفعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is told to give his people the example of the town's people; all commentators, as reported by al-Mawardi, identify the town as Antioch. Qurtubi gives its name as derived from Antabis, its founder, and notes the variant form Antakiyya.
rows.anchor: هذه القرية هي أنطاكية في قول جميع المفسرين فيما ذكر الماوردي. نسبت إلى أهل أنطبيس

rows.speaker: المهدوي
rows.claim: Al-Mahdawi says the town's king was a Pharaoh named Antikhus son of Antikhus who worshipped idols; Abu Ja'far al-Nahhas transmits the account from Ka'b and Wahb.
rows.anchor: وكان بها فرعون يقال له أنطيخس بن أنطيخس يعبد الأصنام ذكره المهدوي

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari names the three envoys Sadiq, Saduq, and Shalum, the third envoy.
rows.anchor: فأرسل الله إليه ثلاثة: وهم صادق، وصدوق، وشلوم هو الثالث. هذا قول الطبري

rows.speaker: غيره
rows.claim: Other commentators name the envoys Shimon and Yohanna.
rows.anchor: وقال غيره: شمعون ويوحنا. وحكى النقاش: سمعان ويحيى

rows.speaker: النقاش
rows.claim: Al-Naqqash gives the names Sam'an and Yahya, without naming Sadiq or Saduq.
rows.anchor: وحكى النقاش: سمعان ويحيى، ولم يذكرا صادقا ولا صدوقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Mathalan” and “ashab al-qarya” may both be direct objects of “strike”; alternatively, “ashab al-qarya” apposes “mathalan” with an omitted “of,” meaning an example of the town's people.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون «مثلا» و «أصحاب القرية» مفعولين لاضرب، أو «أصحاب القرية» بدلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The example warns the Prophet's polytheist audience that the fate of the town's disbelievers may befall them too.
rows.anchor: أمر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بإنذار هؤلاء المشركين أن يحل بهم ما حل بكفار أهل القرية

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view says the two messengers were sent directly by God from the outset.
rows.anchor: قيل: رسل من الله على الابتداء. وقيل: إن عيسى بعثهم إلى أنطاكية للدعاء إلى الله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says Jesus sent them to Antioch by God's command; the verse attributes their mission to God because Jesus acted on His order, after Jesus had been raised to heaven.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن عيسى بعثهم إلى أنطاكية للدعاء إلى الله، وهو قوله تعالى: { إذ أرسلنا إليهم اثنين }

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One account says the townspeople beat and imprisoned the two envoys.
rows.anchor: { فكذبوهما } قيل ضربوهما وسجنوهما. { فعززنا بثالث }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Fa-azzazna” means that God strengthened and reinforced the mission with a third envoy.
rows.anchor: أي فقوينا وشددنا الرسالة «بثالث». وقرأ أبو بكر عن عاصم

rows.speaker: أبو بكر عن عاصم
rows.claim: Abu Bakr from Asim reads the word with a light z; the other readers use the doubled z.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو بكر عن عاصم: «فعززنا بثالث» بالتخفيف وشدد الباقون

rows.speaker: الجوهري
rows.claim: Al-Jawhari says both light and doubled forms mean strengthening; al-Asma'i cites al-Mutalammis's line to attest this usage.
rows.anchor: قال الجوهري: وقوله تعالى: { فعززنا بثالث } يخفف ويشدد أي قوينا وشددنا

rows.speaker: الأصمعي
rows.claim: Al-Asma'i cites a line by al-Mutalammis using “ta'azzaza” for meat becoming stronger or firmer, supporting the readings' shared meaning.
rows.anchor: قال الأصمعي: أنشدني فيه أبو عمرو بن العلاء للمتلمس: أجد إذا رحلت تعزز لحمها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative distinguishes the forms: the light form means to overcome and subdue, as in “wa-azzani fi al-khitab,” while the doubled form means to strengthen and increase.
rows.anchor: التخفيف بمعنى غلبنا وقهرنا ومنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the story, Jesus' two envoys met Habib al-Najjar, the shepherd of a few sheep and the man associated with Surat Ya-Sin; he invited him to God, healed his ill or possessed son by God's permission, and Habib believed. The story identifies him as the man who came from the farthest part of the city.
rows.anchor: فلقيا شيخا يرعى غنيمات له وهو حبيب النجار صاحب «يس» فدعوه إلى الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the envoys healed many sick people, the king summoned them. They identified themselves as Jesus' messengers, offered healing of the congenitally blind, leprous, and sick by God's permission, and called for worship of God alone; the king moved to strike them.
rows.anchor: فأرسل الملك إليهما وكان يعبد الأصنام يستخبرهما فقالا: نحن رسولا عيسى. فقال: وما آيتكما

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb says the king jailed and flogged the two envoys one hundred lashes; when Jesus learned of it, he sent a third.
rows.anchor: وقال وهب: حبسهما الملك وجلدهما مائة جلدة فانتهى الخبر إلى عيسى فأرسل ثالثا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One account identifies the third envoy as Shimon al-Safa, chief of the apostles, sent to support the pair; he befriended the king's court, gained the king's confidence, and feigned agreement with the king's religion before asking about the prisoners.
rows.anchor: قيل: شمعون الصفا رأس الحواريين لنصرهما فعاشر حاشية الملك حتى تمكن منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the story, the envoys healed a blind boy by prayer and clay pupils; the amazed king then asked if they could revive a boy dead for seven days. The envoys prayed openly and Shimon secretly, and the dead boy returned to life, warned the people of the seven fire-filled valleys he had seen, and testified to God, Jesus, and the messengers, naming Shimon the best of them.
rows.anchor: فجيء بغلام ممسوح العينين موضع عينيه كالجبهة، فدعوا ربهما فانشق موضع البصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The revived boy's testimony led Shimon to identify himself as the Messiah's envoy; the king and many people believed, while others disbelieved.
rows.anchor: فأعلمهم شمعون أنه رسول المسيح إليهم، فأثر قوله في الملك، فدعاه إلى الله

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayri says the king believed but his people did not, and Gabriel's cry caused all remaining disbelievers to die.
rows.anchor: وحكى القشيري أن الملك آمن ولم يؤمن قومه، وصاح جبريل صيحة مات كل من بقي منهم من الكفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report says Jesus' envoys worried that they could not speak the town's language; God put them to sleep, angels carried them to Antioch, and they awoke speaking its people's language. The account links this to God's strengthening Jesus with the Holy Spirit.
rows.anchor: روي أن عيسى لما أمرهم أن يذهبوا إلى تلك القرية قالوا: يا نبي الله إنا لا نعرف أن نتكلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The townspeople objected that the envoys were ordinary humans who ate and walked in markets, denied that God sent or commanded anything, and called them liars.
rows.anchor: قالوا مآ أنتم إلا بشر مثلنا } تأكلون الطعام وتمشون في الأسواق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The envoys swear that God knows they were sent and say their only duty is to convey clearly that God is one.
rows.anchor: فقالت الرسل: { ربنا يعلم إنآ إليكم لمرسلون } وإن كذبتمونا { وما علينآ إلا البلاغ المبين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The townspeople say they regarded the messengers as a bad omen.
rows.anchor: قالوا } لهم { إنا تطيرنا بكم } أي تشاءمنا بكم

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Maqatil says rain was withheld from the town for three years, and the people blamed the messengers for the drought.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: حبس عنهم المطر ثلاث سنين فقالوا هذا بشؤمكم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another account says the envoys spent ten years warning the people.
rows.anchor: ويقال: إنهم أقاموا ينذرونهم عشر سنين

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says “we will stone you” means “we will kill you”; he says most Quranic uses of rajm mean killing.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: لنقتلنكم. قال: وعامة ما في القرآن من الرجم معناه القتل

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada understands the threat literally as stoning with rocks.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: هو على بابه من الرجم بالحجارة. وقيل: لنشتمنكم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another gloss is “we will insult you.”
rows.anchor: وقيل: لنشتمنكم وقد تقدم جميعه. { وليمسنكم منا عذاب أليم }

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The painful torment threatened may mean killing, painful punishment, or torment before killing—such as flaying, mutilation, or crucifixion.
rows.anchor: قيل: هو القتل. وقيل: هو التعذيب المؤلم. وقيل: هو التعذيب المؤلم قبل القتل

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says their bad omen is with them: their own share of good and evil remains attached to them, and the messengers are not its source.
rows.anchor: أي شؤمكم معكم أي حظكم من الخير والشر معكم ولازم في أعناقكم، وليس هو من شؤمنا قال معناه الضحاك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the disputatious man as Abdullah ibn Ubayy.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: الإنسان هو عبد الله بن أبي. وقال سعيد بن جبير

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr identifies him as al-As ibn Wa'il al-Sahmi.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: هو العاص بن وائل السهمي. وقال الحسن

rows.speaker: الحسن وابن إسحاق ومالك
rows.claim: Al-Hasan, Ibn Ishaq, and Malik identify him as Ubayy ibn Khalaf al-Jumahi; Ibn Wahb transmits the report from Malik.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: هو أبي بن خلف الجمحي. وقاله ابن إسحاق، ورواه ابن وهب عن مالك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A nutfa is a small amount of water; the verb natafa means to drip.
rows.anchor: وهو اليسير من الماء نطف إذا قطر. { فإذا هو خصيم مبين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He becomes a clear, articulate disputant who presents an argument in controversy, though he had previously been nothing mentioned.
rows.anchor: أي مجادل في الخصومة مبين للحجة. يريد بذلك أنه صار بعد أن لم يكن شيئا مذكورا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the man brought Muhammad a decayed bone and asked whether God could revive it. Muhammad answered yes, saying God would resurrect the questioner and admit him to Hell; the verse was then revealed.
rows.anchor: وذلك أنه أتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بعظم حائل فقال: يا محمد أترى أن الله يحيي هذا بعد ما رم
